research_level: standard (PLAYBOOK 11): 2 photo references (one a surviving piece in an Edo-period house, one a museum reconstruction), one text source for the date

references.i07: data/research_int/refs/i07_edo_nagaya_room.jpg - Fukagawa Edo Museum tenement room (Tenpo-era reconstruction): a two-part isho-dansu, 2 full-width drawers per box, 2 iron ring pulls and an oval lock plate per drawer, iron clasp across the joint, T/L corner fittings, a side carrying handle. Photo DryPot, CC BY 2.5, Wikimedia Commons
references.i01: data/research_int/refs/i01_kasuya_irori.jpg - former Kasuya house (surviving Edo farmhouse, Itabashi): two stacked chests, weathered dusty grey-brown sugi, iron corner plates, vertical bail handle high on the side of the upper box, lock plate. Photo Asanagi, CC0, Wikimedia Commons
references.N06: research/interior/refs_index.json N06 - tansu appear in Osaka in the Kanbun era (1661-73), spread from the Shotoku era (1711-16), costly: T2-3 only in 1730
